title: Nursing Supervisor Reports Staff Fatigue and Caregiver Needs

transcript.speaker: Sana Qureshi
transcript.text: Sana Qureshi, Nursing Supervisor. I’m calling to report a critical staffing issue. About 140 nurses have been on-site for 12 hours or more, and many are exhausted and want to leave, but they can’t because the day shift is still covering and no one is relieving them.

transcript.speaker: Sana Qureshi
transcript.text: We have 30 staff from call-ins, but no one for the PACU overflow. Meals haven’t been provided, and two nurses have called to say they need childcare. I need authorization to act.

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: Understood, Sana. I’m on it. Human Resources is opening the staff care unit for meals, rest, and childcare. We’ll rotate staff out every four hours. I’m approving mandatory overtime up to 14 hours, but no more than that.

transcript.speaker: Carol Beckett
transcript.text: I’m also activating the regional volunteer registry for non-clinical roles — transport, triage assistance, and family support. We’ll bring in travel nurses from the coalition. The PACU overflow will get nurses from the Surgical Pavilion. I’ll confirm with the AOC.

transcript.speaker: Sana Qureshi
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor. I’ll send a team to the staff care unit and coordinate with the volunteer coordinator. We’ll start the rotation now.

instructorNote: This inject tests leadership’s ability to activate staff support systems under extended crisis conditions. Watch for the CNO to engage HR and the regional coalition, and for the AOC to approve overtime and volunteer use.
